items.title: Dick Hyman interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 17, 2001 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: Bucky, who is certainly the best rhythm guitarist I’ve ever played with

ctx.x: And that’s where it began. And of all the people I know that I could be playing with they’re all there for this kind of nice, Count Basie tempo. And that was with Butch and Milt and Bucky. Bucky, who is certainly the best rhythm guitarist I’ve ever played with, he understands time in the same way that Butch and Milt do. And all I did was coast on top of them. We made two takes and they were both so good that we used the first one to open the album and the last one to close it. I’m glad you like it. Thank you.
Yeah. And you talk about Bucky, he has this ability too to put the right note on top of his strumming.

items.title: Bucky Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: By the way you play on one of my new favorite albums, and that is Dick Hyman “The Age of Swing.”

ctx.x: Of course. Schwartz and Dietz, all those songs, “I guess I’ll have to change my plan” and all that stuff. It makes a lot of sense.
By the way you play on one of my new favorite albums, and that is Dick Hyman “The Age of Swing.”
Oh yeah, I like that concept because it has a Count Basie flair to it and that was the whole idea. We did it in New York State.

items.title: Ruth & Bucky Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Saddle River, New Jersey, January 19, 2015
items.q: when I was listening to you talk with Julia and Dick Hyman

ctx.x: No I wouldn’t say that. The way he played, that was great.
And now, when I was listening to you talk with Julia and Dick Hyman, Julia was talking about the studio days and she said to Dick, “you never turned anything down.”
